title: Continuity and the Intermediate Value Theorem

questions.q: State the three conditions that must all hold for $f$ to be continuous at $x=a$.
Determine whether $f(x)=\frac{x^2-4}{x-2}$ (for $x\neq2$, with $f(2)=4$ defined separately) is continuous at $x=2$.
questions.answer: $\lim_{x\to2}f(x) = \lim_{x\to2}(x+2)=4$. Since $f(2)=4$ matches, all three conditions hold: $f$ is continuous at $x=2$.

questions.q: Find $k$ so that $f(x)=kx^2$ for $x\leq2$, and $f(x)=5x-2$ for $x>2$, is continuous at $x=2$.
Find $a$ and $b$ so that $f(x)=2$ for $x\leq-1$, $f(x)=ax+b$ for $-1<x<2$, and $f(x)=6$ for $x\geq2$, is continuous everywhere.
Classify the discontinuity of each function at the indicated point:
answers: Jump — the floor function steps from $1$ to $2$.

questions.q: Show that $f(x)=x^3-3x+1$ has a root in $(0,1)$, using the IVT.
questions.answer: $f(0)=1>0$ and $f(1)=1-3+1=-1<0$. Since $f$ is continuous (a polynomial) and changes sign on $[0,1]$, the IVT guarantees a root in $(0,1)$.

questions.q: A continuous function $g$ satisfies $g(1)=-3$ and $g(5)=7$. Explain why $g$ must take the value $0$ somewhere in $[1,5]$, and state the theorem used.
questions.answer: By the IVT, since $g$ is continuous on $[1,5]$ and $0$ lies between $g(1)=-3$ and $g(5)=7$, there must exist some $c\in[1,5]$ with $g(c)=0$.

questions.q: A cup of coffee's temperature (in $°$C) is a continuous function of time, starting at $90°$C and cooling to $25°$C over 30 minutes. Explain, using the IVT, why the coffee must have been exactly $50°$C at some point.
questions.answer: Temperature is a continuous function of time; since $50$ lies between the starting value $90$ and ending value $25$, the IVT guarantees the temperature equaled $50°$C at some instant during the 30 minutes.

questions.q: Determine the largest interval(s) on which $f(x)=\sqrt{9-x^2}$ is continuous.
questions.answer: The expression under the square root must be non-negative: $9-x^2\geq0 \Rightarrow -3\leq x\leq3$. $f$ is continuous on the closed interval $[-3,3]$.

questions.q: Determine all values of $x$ where $f(x)=\frac{x+1}{x^2-x-6}$ is discontinuous, and classify each discontinuity.
questions.answer: Factor denominator: $x^2-x-6=(x-3)(x+2)$. Discontinuities at $x=3$ and $x=-2$. Since the numerator $x+1$ shares no common factor, both are infinite (vertical asymptote) discontinuities, not removable.

sections.heading: Using the IVT to approximate roots

questions.q: Show that $f(x)=\cos x-x$ has a root in $(0,1)$, then use the IVT with the midpoint to narrow the interval to a length-$0.5$ subinterval.
questions.answer: $f(0)=\cos0-0=1>0$. $f(1)=\cos1-1\approx0.540-1=-0.460<0$. Sign change confirms a root exists in $(0,1)$. Midpoint $x=0.5$: $f(0.5)=\cos(0.5)-0.5\approx0.878-0.5=0.378>0$. Since $f(0.5)>0$ and $f(1)<0$, the root lies in $(0.5,1)$.
